output.question: What is IBM's annual revenue?
output.answer: IBM (International Business Machines, NYSE: IBM) reported revenue of $67.5 billion ($67,535 million) for its most recent full fiscal year, calendar 2025. That was up 8% from $62.75 billion in 2024, or 6% at constant currency. In the first nine months of 2026, revenue was $50.18 billion, compared with $47.85 billion a year earlier. Q3 2026 revenue was $17.1 billion, up 5% (6% at constant currency). From these filed figures, trailing-twelve-month revenue through Q3 2026 works out to about $69.9 billion. On October 21, 2026, IBM said it still expects 2026 revenue to grow 4–5% at constant currency.

key_facts.fact: IBM's full-year 2025 revenue was $67.5 billion ($67,535 million), up 8% (6% at constant currency).
Q3 2026 revenue was $17.1 billion, up 5% (6% at constant currency).
Revenue for the first nine months was $50,182 million in 2026 and $47,849 million in 2025. Derived trailing-twelve-month revenue is 67,535 − 47,849 + 50,182 ≈ $69,868 million.
IBM's 2026 outlook is constant-currency revenue growth of 4–5%, with currency neutral. In January 2026 the outlook had been more than 5%.

passages.quote: Revenue of $67.5 billion, up 8 percent, up 6 percent at constant currency
The company expects full-year constant currency revenue growth of more than 5 percent.
Revenue of $17.1 billion, up 5 percent, up 6 percent at constant currency
The company continues to expect full-year constant currency revenue growth in the range of four-to-five percent.

caveats: The most recent completed fiscal year is 2025. Full-year 2026 results will probably come out in late January 2027.
The roughly $69.9B trailing-twelve-month figure is my own calculation from IBM's reported full-year and nine-month totals. IBM did not report it.

The 2026 growth outlook appears to have been cut from 'more than 5%' in January to '4–5%'. The Q3 release says IBM 'continues to expect' 4–5%, so the cut likely happened at an earlier 2026 quarterly report. I did not check which one.
I took the Q3 nine-month figures from the SEC 8-K exhibit table as a page-reading tool summarized it. I did not check them line by line.
